chunks: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the earnings of the cupper, and he said, 'There is no objection to it.' I said, 'What about the wage of the Tusi?' He said, 'Indeed, the Arabs use it as a standard of value, so there is no objection.'

key_terms.اَلتُّيُوسِ: the Tusi (a type of coin or currency)
key_terms.اَلْحَجَّامِ: the cupper (one who performs cupping therapy)

ai.seo_question: Is the income of a cupper permissible in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the earnings of a cupper (*hijjam*) and specifically accepts the 'Tusi' coin as valid currency based on the principle of customary practice (*urf al-arab*). This highlights the Shia jurisprudential reliance on social convention and recognized monetary standards to determine the validity of wages in commercial transactions.
